You’re spot on… but I’d push this one step further.

It’s not just a *differentiation problem* right now, it’s a **systems problem**.

Most med spas aren’t losing because they look the same… they’re losing because everything *after* the lead looks the same too.

Same slow follow-up  
Same weak consult structure  
Same lack of clear next step  
Same “come back when you’re ready” energy  

So even when they *do* stand out and get attention… they still convert like everyone else.

The ones pulling ahead right now aren’t just saying something different, they’re:
• Engineering a better client journey  
• Controlling the experience from first click to membership  
• And turning each patient into higher LTV instead of chasing more volume  

Price wars happen when there’s no perceived difference.  
But they also happen when the backend can’t support real growth.

Most people don’t need more leads right now… they need to fix what’s happening in between.

Curious if you’ve looked at your numbers from lead → booking → show → plan → retention… that’s where it usually gets interesting.

 Make it to the point: Anyone else feel like it's getting harder to stand out right now?
Every market I talk to, it's the same story. New spa opened up down the street. The one that's been there for 5 years just dropped their Botox price. Everybody's running the same promos, using the same before/afters, saying the same things on their website. And the patients you used to get easily are suddenly shopping around and you're getting a smaller slice of the pie as more competition enters the market.

I hit this wall in my own business recently and had to figure my way out of it, so I wanted to share what I've been working through in case it helps.

18 months ago my calendar was packed. 6-7 week waitlist, couldn't take new clients if I wanted to. Fast forward to this year and it got HARDER to bring people in, even though objectively we'd gotten better at the work.

As I reflected on it, I realized I sounded like every other business out there. Prospects had a hard time picking me over anyone else because it looked like a very similar apples-to-apples comparison. I was trying to win on the margins, hoping people could just tell I was better. News flash....most of them can't and won't. 

I think this is the same trap a lot of med spas are in right now. You might genuinely be better than the place down the street. Your consults are longer. Your technique is different. Your results look more natural. But your website says "Botox & Filler," your ads say "$12/unit," and now you're stuck competing against every other med spa in town on the margins.

A couple things that have helped me start digging out:
Writing out every single thing I do for clients that the competition doesn't. Most of it I was doing for free, in my head, without ever telling anyone it was happening. If it's not said out loud, it doesn't exist to the patient.
Getting specific about WHO I'm for and what outcome I own. "We do Botox and filler" is what everyone says. We need to think bigger on how to differentiate our businesses.
Making sure my proof matches my pitch. If I claim to specialize in something, my reviews, photos, and content better all point to it. Otherwise it's just words.
Is this something you're feeling too? Curious what's working for people right now, or what you've tried that flopped.
